new_entities.name: Semaglutide for PCOS
aliases: semaglutide in obese women with PCOS
GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide for polycystic ovary syndrome
new_entities.description: Use of semaglutide, alone or with metformin, in women with polycystic ovary syndrome to improve weight, metabolic health, menstrual function, or fertility-related outcomes.

new_entities.name: Clinical outcomes
new_entities.description: Clinical outcomes such as weight, insulin resistance, menstrual recovery, fertility, and other patient-centered metabolic or reproductive improvements.

edges.effect_quant: The semaglutide-PCOS literature is still early but directionally favorable. A randomized open-label trial found greater weight loss with semaglutide plus metformin than metformin alone and higher natural pregnancy rates, while smaller semaglutide-specific cohort and pilot studies report substantial weight reduction, menstrual improvement, and better metabolic markers.
edges.population: overweight or obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome, often with insulin resistance, prediabetes, or prior failure of lifestyle therapy alone
edges.mechanism: Semaglutide likely improves PCOS outcomes indirectly through weight loss, appetite reduction, and improved insulin sensitivity, which can lower hyperandrogenic and inflammatory burden and help restore menstrual or fertility-related function.
edges.summary: This is a promising protective edge, but it is not yet as mature as the metformin or broader anti-androgen evidence base in PCOS. The clinical signal is strong enough to capture, especially for obesity-linked PCOS, while staying explicit that the literature is still developing.
edges.caveats: Most data are from small or open-label studies, often in obese PCOS populations and sometimes alongside metformin. Generalization to lean PCOS or to long-term reproductive outcomes should be cautious.

evidence.citation: MinggeY et al 2025 Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
evidence.notes: Effects of combined metformin and semaglutide therapy on body weight, metabolic parameters, and reproductive outcomes in overweight/obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a prospective, randomized, controlled, open-label clinical trial.

effect_quant.comparator: natural pregnancy rate from weeks 16 to 40 with semaglutide plus metformin versus metformin alone in overweight or obese women with PCOS (35% vs 15%)

evidence.notes: Semaglutide Treatment of Excessive Body Weight in Obese PCOS Patients Unresponsive to Lifestyle Programs.

effect_quant.comparator: mean body-weight change after 6 months of semaglutide treatment in obese women with PCOS who responded to therapy

evidence.notes: Effect of semaglutide with metformin for weight loss and fertility in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) patients with obesity: A pilot prospective study.

effect_quant.comparator: patients achieving pregnancy during follow-up after semaglutide plus metformin therapy in obese women with PCOS and prediabetes

evidence.notes: The metabolic benefits associated with semaglutide use in obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome- a retrospective study of clinical practice.

effect_quant.comparator: mean weight change after more than 6 months of semaglutide therapy in routine clinical practice among obese women with PCOS
